newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Malaysia no longer front-runner for alumina plant.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia no longer front-runner for alumina plant.

text.p: Malaysia is no longer clear favourite to be the home for a proposed A$1 billion (US$760 million) alumina refinery after its Australian developer, Comalco Ltd, on Monday looked closer to home.
Comalco said it had agreed to look at building the refinery in the north Australian state of Queensland, powered by natural gas piped in from neighbouring Papua New Guinea.
Queensland and Malaysia's Sarawak state have long been competing to be chosen as Comalco's site for the refinery, which Comalco says may later be expanded into a A$3.5 billion project.
Comalco has said it is leaning toward Sarawak, based on its edge in terms of security and pricing of natural gas supplies.
But on Monday the aluminium producer said it was looking at the prospect of a Queensland-based refinery fuelled by gas supplied along the proposed Papua New Guinea-Australia pipeline.

The A$3 billion pipeline has been proposed by U.S. oil major Chevron Corp and would take gas 2,400 km (1,500 miles) from the Kutubu gas field in Papua New Guinea's remote Southern Highlands to Queensland via Torres Strait.
"Comalco and Chevron recognise that the two projects are, to an extent, interdependent," the companies said in a joint statement to the Australian stock exchange.
Later, a Comalco spokesman told Reuters the Chevron gas pipeline had put Queensland's Gladstone site back in the race against Sarawak to become the refinery's home.
"Gladstone was lagging behind Malaysia and it was because of this energy issue, amongst others. But this is certainly bringing Gladstone back into contention," said Comalco spokesman Greg Walker.
The refinery is to be commissioned in year 2001 and produce annually about 1.4 million tonnes of alumina, but Comalco says it could be expanded later to over 4.2 million tonnes.
The gas pipeline is also hoped to come on line in 2001.
Comalco is owned 67 percent by Anglo-Australian mining giant, Rio Tinto Plc/Ltd.
